clue.text: Celebrity limits retiring astronaut

indicators.note: something retiring draws back, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: a celebrity is a name, a well-known person
caps are limits, as in a spending cap

explanation.surface: A star restricts a shy space traveller, or a famous person's limits fade away.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceman is an informal word for someone who travels in space, a synonym of astronaut.

clue.text: Track lacking nothing by extremely trendy Spice Girl

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a spoor is an animal's track
O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A very fashionable pop star with no track record.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a British girl group; Mel C was nicknamed Sporty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporty Spice was the nickname of Melanie Chisholm in the 1990s pop group.

clue.text: Come into use as American soldiers turn up without protection against disease

indicators.note: without means outside, so these letters go round the next piece
in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, soldiers
PPE is personal protective equipment, worn against infection

explanation.surface: US troops arrive with no vaccines or masks against illness.
explanation.definitionFit: When a new word or product appears it emerges and starts being used.

clue.text: Die to have Adams' earliest books on space by the way

indicators.note: on means placed next to, joining the pieces

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
to pass, or pass away, is to die

indicators.note: the earliest letter is the first

parts.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A writer must die to have his first books shelved on space travel.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printing measure, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: En passant is a French phrase used in English to mean incidentally, in passing.

clue.text: Applying to all provision of meals after cook chats with Rose

indicators.note: the meals piece comes after the rearranged letters
to cook figures is to falsify them, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
board is meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Meals arranged once the chef has a word with someone called Rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like a noun for the chef but signals rearranging CHATS and ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Across the board means affecting everyone or everything in a group equally.

clue.text: Number six starts to rant guiltily at the Italian linesman

parts.note: six in Roman numerals is VI

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words give their opening letters

parts.note: il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A footballer wearing number six shouts guiltily at an Italian assistant referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' suggests football, but here it means a writer of lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil, the Roman poet of the Aeneid, wrote lines of verse, so he is a linesman in the crossword sense.

clue.text: Most suitable stuffing inside already

indicators.note: the answer is stuffed within these words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The best stuffing has already gone inside the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect, the best possible choice for a purpose.

clue.text: Bishop in Georgia is against making place fortified

indicators.note: the bishop goes in, inside the next letters

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
on can mean against, as in an attack on someone

explanation.surface: A bishop in the Caucasus opposes building a fort.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a town or post with troops stationed in it to defend it.

clue.text: Say nothing in return about daughter's delayed departure

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
nil is nothing
re means about or concerning
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter keeps silent about her slow leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay longer than expected before leaving, so lingered means was slow to go.

clue.text: Flyer showing various retro bread bins

indicators.note: various means of differing kinds, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leaflet advertising assorted vintage bread bins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' looks like a leaflet but means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin redbreast is a common European bird, and any bird is a flyer.

clue.text: Expert essentially protected by new apron in theory

indicators.note: something protected by another sits inside it, so these letters go within
new signals the letters of apron are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central part, its middle two letters

explanation.surface: A chef's expert theory about a fresh pinafore keeping him clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apron' looks like part of the kitchen scene, but it is only letters to rearrange; 'in theory' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that works on paper is sound in principle though untested in practice.

clue.text: Left remaining ladder in area beyond airstrip

parts.note: food left remaining is left over
a run is a ladder in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: A ladder left lying about in the area past the end of a runway.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder here is the British word for a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: An overrun is the paved stretch past a runway's end, used if an aircraft fails to stop in time.

clue.text: Taunt, reportedly swallowing last of pear drops

indicators.note: what swallows takes the next piece inside itself
reportedly means as heard, so we need a word that sounds like the synonym

parts.note: to taunt is to tease

indicators.note: the final letter of the next word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mocking someone while they eat their pear drops, the boiled sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Pear drops are British boiled sweets, but 'drops' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tears are drops of liquid from the eyes, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Undisturbed by story about feminine type of painting

parts.note: still water is undisturbed

indicators.note: about means around, so the story wraps the next letter

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
F is the grammar abbreviation for feminine

explanation.surface: A calm story about a woman, then a genre of art.
explanation.definitionFit: A still life is a genre of painting depicting arranged objects such as fruit or flowers.

clue.text: Gain control over city capturing rebel leader of coup

parts.note: to master something is to gain control over it

indicators.note: the city takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent is an English city, often just Stoke

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rebel seizes a city and takes power in a political coup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coup' looks like a political takeover in the surface but means a brilliant stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterstroke is a brilliant move, as is a coup in the sense of a clever success.

clue.text: Entice frustratingly awkward Titans with ale

indicators.note: awkward signals clumsily arranged letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clumsy giants lure people with beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to tease with something desirable kept out of reach, like Tantalus.

clue.text: Like Uriah perhaps after son's feeling embarrassment from shame

indicators.note: in a down clue, after means the next piece comes below the son

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
Uriah Heep is the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A boy feels shame after acting like a creepy Dickens villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepish describes looking awkward and embarrassed after doing something wrong.

clue.text: Chinese lawyer primarily looking into death of textile producer

parts.note: the Han are the main ethnic group of China

indicators.note: the letter looks into, so it goes inside the next word

parts.note: doom is death or ruin

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Chinese lawyer investigates a death in a mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A handloom is a manually operated weaving machine, which produces cloth.

clue.text: Become widely discussed online during trial causing great distress

indicators.note: during puts one thing within the span of another

parts.note: a hearing is a trial in court
to trend is to become a popular topic on social media

explanation.surface: A court case goes viral online and upsets everyone involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heartrending is so sad that it seems to tear the heart, causing anguish.

clue.text: Landed property in the middle of Donegal say

indicators.note: the central letter of the next word

parts.note: taken as written
to state is to say

explanation.surface: An estate somewhere in central Donegal, the Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large piece of land with a house, owned as property.

clue.text: Fellow, under pressure, putting on a monkey suit

indicators.note: putting on means adding, so the fellow is attached
the pressure goes under the cover of the monkey, inside it

parts.note: an ape is a monkey in the loose sense
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
Al is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man, stressed, dresses up in a gorilla costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monkey suit' reads as a costume, but 'suit' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is a petition or plea, which is what an appeal also is.

clue.text: Undertaking, in French, to quickly read boxing article

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the article goes inside

parts.note: to devour a book is to read it eagerly and fast
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A task in French: to race through a book about boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an attempt or enterprise, the noun sense of an undertaking.

clue.text: Camus oddly dismissed study by poet

indicators.note: the odd letters go, leaving the alternate even ones

parts.note: taken as written
a den is a study, a private room

explanation.surface: A French writer is oddly dropped from the reading list for a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Put forward by a left-leaning teller of stories

indicators.note: in an across clue, leaning to the left means reading from right to left

parts.note: to pose a question is to put it forward

explanation.surface: A political view proposed by a socialist storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-leaning' seems political but tells you to read POSE and A backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of fables, short moral tales.

clue.text: Working OK

explanation.walkthrough: Two short senses of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a machine in good repair and also a proper or permissible action.

clue.text: Make lively Hindu queen run off with ship's officer

indicators.note: the run goes off, so it is removed

parts.note: a rani is the wife of a rajah, a Hindu queen
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A queen elopes with an officer from a ship, livening things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to bring to life or enliven, giving energy to something.

clue.text: Kind of soldier wearing shades for the most part

indicators.note: the colours are worn by the soldier, so they enclose him
most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: shades are hues, tints of colour
a man is a soldier of the lower ranks

explanation.surface: A type of soldier who mostly wears sunglasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of soldier' reads as one phrase, but 'Kind' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means compassionate, the adjective sense of kind.

clue.text: Extremely delicate repair of leather around end of banquette

indicators.note: the reworked leather goes round the next letter
repair means making again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Restoring the fragile leather on the end of an upholstered bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair of' turns LEATHER into ETHERAL, and E, the end of 'banquette', goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means so light and fine as to seem not of this world.
